questions.question: Company X uses a job-order costing system. At the end of the year, manufacturing overhead applied was $450,000, while actual manufacturing overhead incurred was $480,000. If the underapplied overhead is considered material and allocated among Work in Process, Finished Goods, and Cost of Goods Sold based on their ending balances of $100,000, $200,000, and $700,000 respectively, what is the adjusted ending balance of Cost of Goods Sold?

During its first year of operations, Delta Co. produced 10,000 units and sold 8,000 units. Costs incurred were: Direct materials $5/unit, Direct labor $3/unit, Variable manufacturing overhead $2/unit, Fixed manufacturing overhead $50,000 total, Variable selling and administrative $1/unit, and Fixed selling and administrative $20,000 total. What is the difference in operating income between absorption costing and variable costing?
options: Absorption costing operating income is $10,000 higher than variable costing operating income.
Variable costing operating income is $10,000 higher than absorption costing operating income.
Absorption costing operating income is $4,000 higher than variable costing operating income.
Variable costing operating income is $4,000 higher than absorption costing operating income.

questions.question: Sigma Corp. uses the weighted-average method in its process costing system. The Assembly Department started the month with 2,000 units in beginning work-in-process inventory. During the month, 10,000 units were started. At month-end, 3,000 units remained in ending work-in-process (40% complete as to conversion costs). Direct materials are added at the beginning of the process, while conversion costs are incurred uniformly throughout. What are the equivalent units of production (EUP) for direct materials and conversion costs, respectively?
options: 10,000 for direct materials and 9,000 for conversion costs
12,000 for direct materials and 11,400 for conversion costs
9,000 for direct materials and 10,200 for conversion costs
12,000 for direct materials and 10,200 for conversion costs

questions.question: In financial reporting using XBRL (eXtensible Business Reporting Language), which of the following best describes an 'instance document'?
options: A document that defines the specific visual layout and formatting of financial reports for web display.
A computer-readable file containing actual financial facts and figures tagged with elements from a taxonomy.
A standardized dictionary containing all accounting concepts and definitions approved by regulatory bodies.
A custom taxonomy extension developed by an enterprise to report non-standard financial transactions.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a key structural feature of Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB) compared to traditional incremental budgeting?
options: Prior year expense allocations serve as the baseline and are automatically adjusted for anticipated inflation.
Every department head must justify all proposed expenditures from a zero baseline for each budget period using decision packages.
Budget allocations are fixed for multi-year capital projects rather than evaluated on an annual basis.
Total budgeted costs automatically adjust in direct proportion to changes in operational volume during the period.
